mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and earnings estimates are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of months following a 1% INDPRO drop, indicating markets are shrugging off supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, signaling a weakening labor market, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending slows and earnings estimates are cut.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and retail sales remain strong following the UNRATE increase, indicating the labor market weakening is not impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs pressure corporate profits.
failure_condition: Equity market volatility, as measured by the VIX, fails to rise above 20 following the Fed rate hike, indicating markets are not overly concerned about the tightening.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, signaling a weakening housing market, consumer-related sectors will underperform and drag the S&P 500 lower over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks outperform the broader market following the drop in housing starts, indicating the weakness is not impacting consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, signaling a weakening labor market, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as earnings estimates are revised downward.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth slows by > 100k jobs/mo for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fail to rise following the payroll slowdown, indicating the labor market weakening is not leading to increased layoffs.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending (RSAFS) accelerates by more than 1% month-over-month, signaling strong consumer demand, cyclical sectors will outperform and drive the S&P 500 higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer discretionary sector underperforms the broader market following the RSAFS acceleration, indicating the spending surge is not boosting cyclical stocks.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3% and the Fed funds rate is below 2%, indicating the Fed is behind the curve on inflation, real yields will rise and S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 60 trading days as equities are pressured by the prospect of tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: Real yields fail to rise following the inflation overshoot and Fed funds rate divergence, indicating markets do not expect a significant monetary policy response.
